speaker: rickhilderley
text: Yes, first of all, I had a public comment in any of our virtual meetings. So well done, Kevin. And I know, Devin, you're there in the background. So great job in making sure that that went well. Thank you. I provided a memo with my recommendation on the issue of reconfiguration. And I won't read it word for word, but there are some talking points in it that I wanna stress in making this recommendation. First of all, the primary goals that I am trying to focus on currently and will be continuing to focus on moving forward through the next several weeks. So my recommendation is a partial implementation of the reconfiguration plan with these guiding principles. First of all, keep as many students in the last building they were familiar with as possible. I've heard this, and I believe that it's very important that when we are able to come back with face-to-face instruction at some point, and I believe that we will be able to do that at some point during the 2020 and 21 school year, when we do that, this plan assures that except for one group, that would be the current eighth graders who would naturally move to the high school, the rest of them would be staying in the building that they were most familiar with when the pandemic put us out of school last March. Next, focus the majority of our time and effort this summer on the training and preparation of teachers for distance learning with, of course, increased rigor and the planning of new safety protocols in the event of a return to face-to-face instruction. That process is going to take an enormous amount of our time. Next, increasing the capacity of all families to engage in online instruction. Later, I will talk about a process that we are involved in now that is going to try to gather some information and provide an opportunity for members of our staff to help us plan what next year might look like. And some of the information we're going to need in detail is families who are not able to engage currently with online instruction. We need to find that out and we need to address it. We want to try to reduce anxiety in students while increasing their potential for success regardless of what our instructional platform is. We want to develop sensible curriculum and delivery decisions in all of the areas. And we obviously need to consider the realities of a significantly reduced budget. And all the while, promoting our unique readiness for virtual learning to all area families. Our virtual academy is well-prepared to make offerings to maybe families who aren't choosing to come see at this time. And we want to ramp up our promotion of those activities. I recommend the following items that we would move second grade to the ELCs as planned. Students would then roll up and remain in the building that they last attended. The current eighth grade students would move to Tecumseh High School and the Herrick Park building would remain empty for the 2020 and 21 school year. The current seventh grade students would remain at West in the Patterson building for eighth grade. The staff would remain with them. Current sixth grade students would remain at Compass for seventh grade, the seventh grade program. The teachers would need to move to the Compass building where they will eventually end up anyway. TPS administration will then have to revisit the staffing plan and make necessary adjustments. We had created a staffing plan based on the full move that we would have to take some time to look at where some of those moves could take place and where they wouldn't be able to take place at this time. Eventually, when students and teachers can return for in-person instruction, students will return to a place that's familiar with many familiar faces. It's critical that our efforts between now and when school does resume in whatever capacity that we spend a lot of time in preparing teachers for whatever the landscape is in education. During our current continuity of learning plan, we addressed online instruction relatively lightly because of the parameters of the governor's orders. With increased rigor, with accountability, grading, tests, full attendance requirements, the online environment will look much different in the fall. And we need to spend time with staff to prepare them. The move would require us to also do that in an environment where staff members weren't entirely familiar with each other. This leaves staff members in their current relationships, current building leadership, grade level curriculum familiarity. And I believe that that gives them the strongest ability to be prepared and successful. We plan to make full reconfiguration the following year with the grade levels in the buildings that we eventually want them in. But at this time, my recommendation is to make consideration of the training needs of the staff and most especially the social emotional needs of our students. So those are my recommendations. Later, it will come up as an action item. And if there are questions, we can discuss them at that time.

speaker: rickhilderley
text: All right, thank you. There are a couple of bullet points on your agenda and a few more that I'll add in. First of all, President Johnson asked for some information about GASB 84, which GASB is an acronym, G-A-S-B. It stands for Governmental Accounting Standards Board. And 84 refers to a statement that came out in 2018 about governmental accounting standards. And because schools are essentially governmental agencies, then aspects of that statement have to do with schools. In this case, it has specifically to do with what have always been referred to as activity accounts. And those activity accounts can include PTO, special fundraisers, sports teams, and their activity accounts, all of those things. For years, those accounts stood outside of the district's general fund, and were not part of the yearly audit. The GASB 84 statement and ruling says that now those funds must be part of either the general fund or a special fund under the guidance of the school district. So essentially, all of the money that comes and goes throughout the district has to be audited the same way. So it requires training. And Kevin has asked about training, not only for the administration, but for the board. There are two groups that we work with quite closely, and one that we're a member of, one that we retain. The Michigan Association of School Boards has a training platform for GASB 84, as does TRUN, our school law firm. So either of those would be adequate for bringing information to the board, and also making sure that the administration is up to date on those accounting practices. And I'll be happy to bring forward either one of those at any time. It's been in place since September of last year, so we're relatively familiar with it, but certainly making board members more formally aware of it would be very appropriate. Next is childcare program. We've made a statement that the childcare program is down for the summer. However, there are some circumstances coming up in August where we may have some flexibility to provide childcare for frontline workers. We will explore that as we get closer to that time, but Joanne Leip has advised me that they would be interested in being a part of that, but we don't know just exactly how that would work. I have said, and I'm throwing a blanket statement out there that we're not doing the childcare program this summer, but there is some circumstances under which we could provide those services. So I just want to advise the board that you may hear more about this later on. This item actually could have come up under good news, but I want to advise the board and anybody watching, the local radio station WLEN has offered 15 minutes of airtime free to each district to have graduation speeches. And we are in the process of recording those. I did my recording today. Mr. Mills has an introductory statement, and then we have our class president, our valedictorian and salutatorian who are all speaking. And then I have a couple of minutes of closing comments in that 15 minute window. They don't know exactly when that's going to air, but we will be promoting it to the district and I'll inform the board members when they have their schedule out there. All of the districts in Lenawee County are being given a specific time to listen. So that was a very nice, I think, community outreach thing that WLEN did for the county. I want to announce that our distance learning action team is being put together this week. We met administratively today. Jacob Anastasov has done a nice job in coordinating that effort. We're going to enlist the help of staff members to design what school might look like. I think it's most assuredly going to involve some version of online instruction. And we've learned a lot about things that have gone well through this continuity of learning plan. And we've learned things that we would like to do differently, certain ways that we want to organize our materials, and then also the gaps in training that everybody is going to have to fill. So we will have another meeting tomorrow to complete that organization process. And then we're calling this week zero as we get ourselves prepared. And then we'll start those meetings next week with staff broken down into different categories. Once we have that process organized, I'll share that information with board members. And then I mentioned the Building Futures Committee last week. I didn't have the specific date. June 2nd is the first date of the Building Futures Committee. It's followed very closely after that with another meeting on June 9th. We know right now that the June 2nd meeting will be a virtual meeting. It's introductory and gives people an overview of what the task of the group will be. So I think that that holds pretty well in the virtual environment. And then we will make decisions about how we might approach an in-person meeting in ways that we could distance people in a large space. So moving forward with it right now and we'll see how it goes meeting by meeting. I think that that's it for my report.
